newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds up amid down-in-coupon trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds up amid down-in-coupon trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backeds posted moderate advances Monday, with premium coupons underperforming amid growing concern that prepayments will soon accelerate.
Current coupon 7-1/2-percent bonds from all three agencies were up 10/32, matching the price increase in 10-year Treasuries. Higher coupons were up 1/8 to 1/4 point.
As interest rates continued to slide, and prepayment risks rose, traders saw a shift from eight to 9-1/2 percent coupons to the safer haven of current and discount coupons.
Thirty-year Treasuries yielded 6.58 percent late Monday, four basis points closer to the 6.50 percent prepay trigger.

"The 8-1/2s are definitely refiable (refinanceable) and the eights will probably pick up in refis soon," one trader said. "We'll see it in September's (prepayment) numbers. Most people don't hear about (lower mortgage rates) right away."
Among key issues, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7-1/2 percent coupons were up 10/32 at 101-16/32 bid, yielding 98 basis points over 10-year Treasuries. That spread was unchanged from late Thursday.
Comparable Fannie Maes and Freddie Macs were also up 10/32, at 101-11/32 and 101-16/32, respectively.
The 7-1/2 coupons have been market leaders, bolstered by institutional investor prepayment concerns and a reach for yield by retail investors, traders said.

The 7-1/2s won't be hurt immediately by prepayments. But traders said yield spreads above Treasuries could widen on 7-1/2s along with higher coupons. That would be a retracement of the relatively strong performance of the 7-1/2s.

Thursday's Mortgage Bankers Association index could foreshadow a refinancing pick-up. A more prolonged low-rate environment will alter the current benign prepayment trend more sharply later, market participants said.
